answer: Each identity stakes a 70-credit bond and files one ferrous load record, key-signed so it cannot be transferred. The record enters one shale stratum of a public ledger, and an auditor recomputes each stratum total. A filing past its zenith capacity, or the same load filed twice, burns the bond. The fee starts at 25 and rises by 4 per filing, so the 1000th pays 4021; 1000 fakes lock 70000 and pay 2023000. A rented-load ring fails because the ledger exposes the reused load key and burns each bond. An honest identity files once, pays 25, and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
